what: End-to-end smoke test of the Phase 2b train.py argv on a two-language mini corpus (afr + deu, 500 lines each, copied from wili_corpus_shared) with the patched fp64 spm_train, for the two bases rebuilt under the author's 2026-08-23 dropped-entry decision. Same argv as slurm_wili_train_llm_tokenizer.sh, then convert.py, then analysis.inspect_variant_models.

decision.statement: For LLM tokenizers whose vocabularies contain entries the per-language SentencePiece seed-vocab writer refuses (raw tab, newline or carriage return; UNILID/unilid/vocab_io.py:119-120), the offending entries are DROPPED WHOLE from the converted base vocabulary. Nothing is stripped, sanitized or re-encoded.
decision.supersedes: the BLOCKED branches of slurm_wili_train_llm_tokenizer.sh and the FAIL rows of outputs/rerelease/wili_phase2_conversion_smoke.json

filter_fidelity.predicate_mirrored: UNILID/unilid/vocab_io.py:119  ('\t' in t) or ('\n' in t) or ('\r' in t)
filter_fidelity.specials_skipped: UNILID/unilid/vocab_io.py:113,117-118 (the four UNILID specials); none was flagged in either vocabulary
filter_fidelity.checked_against_real_writer: every dropped token was passed to the real _write_sp_seed_vocab_file and confirmed to raise 'Token contains tab/newline'; the surviving vocabulary was passed through it in one call and confirmed accepted
filter_fidelity.identity_rebuild: rebuilding the converted base with an EMPTY drop set reproduced train.py:_convert_to_unigram_base's own output byte for byte, for both models
filter_fidelity.inertness_no_offending_entries: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B converted WITH the flag gives sha256 52773b2470a130d50c4b7556d626005b531af47ed88a0578ad989485c5744703, identical to the pre-existing base recorded in the case table
filter_fidelity.inertness_flag_off: mistral-community/Mistral-7B-v0.2 converted WITHOUT the flag gives sha256 1e59ff82a41f50fdc398996662bd29f1e4ec60e11aac18f28602054cc2b5caa3, identical to the pre-drop base; only an added non-fatal WARNING on stderr differs

finding: Both rows now train, pack and inspect clean. The per-language SentencePiece path no longer reaches the vocab_io.py:119 refusal for either model; base_tokenizer_reused is true, real-token mass is 1.0 and the special-token defect is absent in both. What the dropped entries cost is coverage of literal carriage returns inside a token, which the corpus writer strips per line anyway; nothing else about the two models changes.
not_submitted: The full 235-language jobs were NOT submitted; the sbatch commands are in the handoff.
note_byte_level: --byte-level is passed by the job script but is NOT what is used: language_specific_trainer.py:263 takes the byte-level setting from the base tokenizer and logs 'regardless of user input: byte-level=False' for both of these SentencePiece-style bases. That was true before the dropped-entry decision too.
